passages.provision_quote: On conviction of an offense under this article, the judge shall enter an order that requires the person to return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States or the person's nation of origin.
passages.note: Bill text page: the measure bundles public-benefit document fraud, SAVE verification, lethal-fentanyl sentencing, illegal entry with return orders, and e-verify fraud.
Bill history page: prime sponsor is Toma, and it prints the House final tally but names no individual voter.
House Final Reading roll call: Gillette is the only member of that surname on the list, and 29 No votes keep it well clear of near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Gillette voted Y on final passage of HCR2060 (2024), the referred "Secure the Border Act", which creates a state illegal-entry offense and orders a convicted alien to "return to the foreign nation from which the person entered or attempted to enter the United States". The measure carries unrelated subjects alongside illegal entry — public-benefit document fraud, SAVE verification, a lethal-fentanyl sentencing enhancement and e-verify fraud — so under the vote ladder a Y on final passage shows only the enforcement side unless his own words tie the vote to the removal clause. It does not establish "Focus deportation on recent arrivals while leaving long-settled undocumented immigrants in place" either: the act's prospective-only limit on the new state crime says nothing about leaving long-settled immigrants in place, and silence is not a clause.
